content: Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist to avoid potential drug interactions. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as stool sample tests, to monitor your progress. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing them in the bathroom. Liquid medication should be kept in its original bottle and refrigerated. Discard any unused liquid medication after 12 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of expired or unused medication. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, or stomach/abdominal pain. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience any unusual or severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately. Before taking fidaxomicin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Fidaxomicin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current formulary information, as individual plans and formulary details may vary.
